prompt: What is the difference between map() and flatMap() in streams?
choices: map() works on lists; flatMap() works on arrays
map() transforms each element to one result; flatMap() transforms each element to a stream and flattens them
map() is terminal; flatMap() is intermediate
explanation: map(f) produces a Stream<R> where each element is transformed by f. flatMap(f) expects f to return a Stream for each element, then merges all those streams into one. Use flatMap to flatten a stream of lists.
